package_info.package_manager: Unknown (malware distributed via supply chain attack, not a public package repository)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (malware variant, not versioned as a package)
package_info.why_malicious: ICONICSTEALER is an infostealer malware variant used in a supply chain attack against 3CX’s Software. It is designed to exfiltrate sensitive information from infected systems, communicating with attacker-controlled C2 servers. Its deployment via a trusted software supply chain makes it particularly dangerous and deceptive.

execution_context.file_location: Injected into 3CX software binary or loaded as a malicious DLL

malicious_snippets.code_language: javascript (or compiled binary, actual language may be C++/C#/Go)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects browser credentials and system information, then sends this data to a remote C2 server, resulting in credential and information exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code reads sensitive credential stores and system information, then transmits this data to an external server, which is a hallmark of infostealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not access browser credential stores or exfiltrate user/system data to unknown remote servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise endpoint management tools may collect system information for inventory purposes, but should not access browser credentials or send data to untrusted domains.

malicious_snippets.code_language: javascript (or compiled binary, actual language may be C++/C#/Go)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends collected data to a hardcoded C2 server via HTTP POST, enabling remote exfiltration of sensitive information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Hardcoded C2 domains and exfiltration of sensitive data are classic signs of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal application modules should not communicate with unknown external servers, especially to transmit sensitive data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or crash reporting may send limited, anonymized data to trusted vendor servers, but not credentials or sensitive user data.

attack_chain.action: Malicious ICONICSTEALER code is injected into or bundled with a legitimate 3CX software update via supply chain compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code on end-user systems

attack_chain.action: When the compromised 3CX software is executed, the malicious module runs in the context of the trusted application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of credentials and system information

attack_chain.action: Collected credentials and system information are transmitted to attacker-controlled C2 infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive data to attackers

behavioral_signatures: Legitimate application processes accessing browser credential stores
Unexpected network connections to untrusted or hardcoded C2 domains
Exfiltration of system or credential data via HTTP POST
file_indicators: Unexpected DLLs or modules loaded by 3CX process
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to known malicious C2 domains associated with ICONICSTEALER
Unusual data transfer patterns from 3CX application processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for 3CX or other trusted application processes accessing browser credential stores or making outbound connections to suspicious domains. Use EDR solutions to detect unexpected module loads or binary modifications. Correlate network traffic with known C2 indicators and flag anomalous data exfiltration attempts.
